title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for teens with enhanced safety controls and halts model development due to cyber risks
summary: OpenAI unveils a version of ChatGPT designed for minors with usage limits and educational tools, while admitting that cybersecurity risks force a slowdown in the launch of new models.

title: Intel prepares Nova Lake and Razor Lake with up to 28 cores and TSMC N2X node to compete with AMD Ryzen X3D in laptops
summary: Intel's future CPUs will reach base frequencies of 3.4 GHz with 24 cores and use TSMC's 2 nm lithography, while Razor Lake will integrate 3D cache to rival AMD's X3D.

title: ASUS and HYDRA launch monitoring and power limit solutions for the RTX 50's 12V-2×6 connector after overheating reports
summary: Manufacturers and tool developers implement per-pin monitoring, automatic overcurrent shutdown, and unlocked VRAM controls to mitigate risks of the new power connector.

title: Apple accidentally leaks its AirPods with built-in camera: they will serve as Siri's eyes for environmental recognition
summary: A macOS update and leaked videos reveal that the next AirPods will include cameras for Siri to identify objects and environments, dismissing fears of voyeuristic use.

title: Anthropic CEO warns that AI centralizes power and calls for regulation of companies like his to avoid chip concentration
summary: Dario Amodei states that AI tends to concentrate power in whoever controls the hardware and proposes external regulation, while his company multiplies revenue sevenfold to $65 billion annualized.

title: Linux 7.2 arrives with cache-aware scheduling, Btrfs improvements, Apple M3 support, and full HDMI 2.1 on Radeon
summary: The new kernel optimizes CPU cache usage, accelerates the Btrfs filesystem, adds support for Apple M3 chips, and enables HDMI 2.1 on AMD Radeon graphics cards.

title: Department of Justice investigates Andreessen Horowitz for board seats at competing AI companies
summary: The inquiry examines whether the venture capital firm's partners breach fiduciary duties by sitting on the boards of rival AI startups.

title: Cursor launches Origin, a code hosting platform to compete with GitHub by leveraging developer frustration
summary: The AI-assisted code editor presents its own git repository service with native review and collaboration features, positioning itself as a direct alternative to GitHub.

title: Noctua rejects RGB lighting, screens, and white colors: its engineers prioritize performance and reliability over aesthetics
summary: The Austrian manufacturer confirms it will not follow market trends like RGB or white casings, dedicating resources to thermal and acoustic optimization of its fans and heatsinks.

title: YouTube changes its view counter: now counts a play from the first frame, inflating public metrics
summary: The platform will modify its methodology to count views at the start of the video instead of after 30 seconds, which will artificially inflate audience figures.

title: Microsoft allows laptops with only 8 GB RAM in Windows 11 exempting them from Copilot+ requirements, but manufacturers raise prices up to 500%
summary: The relaxation of hardware requirements for basic devices leads to drastic price increases, while the lightweight version of Windows 11 omits AI features like Recall.

title: ASUS unveils ROG Raikiri II Pro controller with LCD screen, TMR joysticks, 8,000 Hz polling, and 79-hour battery
summary: The new PC controller includes a customizable screen, Hall effect sticks, ultra-high polling rate, and extended battery life, positioning itself as a premium gaming option.

title: Sony delays PlayStation 6 beyond 2027: CEO admits they cannot survive current scenario without changes
summary: Hiroki Totoki confirms that the next console will not arrive in 2027 as expected, citing economic pressures and the need to rethink the business model.

title: Apple reduces commissions and relaxes rules for alternative stores in the EU after regulatory pressure
summary: The company adjusts its App Store fees and allows direct links to external payments in European apps, complying with the Digital Markets Act.
